title: Casting Lots
lead: Israel often made decisions by lot, trusting God to guide the result: to divide the land, choose the goat for the Day of Atonement, find a guilty man (if, as is usually assumed, a lot was used there), or fill Judas's place among the apostles (Leviticus 16:8; Joshua 14:2; Joshua 7:14; Acts 1:26; Proverbs 16:33).

sections.b: A lot (goral) was a marked stone or stick drawn from a container or cast down. Aaron casts lots over two goats (Leviticus 16:8–10). The land is divided by lot (Numbers 26:55–56; Joshua 14–19), and the same word comes to mean one's share in life (Psalm 16:5–6). Lots, or a similar sacred device, single out Achan and Jonathan and pick Saul as king (Joshua 7:14–18; 1 Samuel 14:41–42; 1 Samuel 10:20–21). Those passages say only that a tribe, clan or man is "taken," and 1 Samuel 14:41 names the Thummim, so the device may have been the Urim and Thummim rather than a goral. Lots also settle the sailors' question in Jonah 1:7. Haman's lot, pur, gives Purim its name (Esther 3:7; 9:24–26). Soldiers cast lots for Jesus' clothes (Psalm 22:18; John 19:24), and the apostles choose Matthias by lot (Acts 1:26). After Pentecost the New Testament never mentions lots again.
